UY Punong Panlalawigan Province of Zamboanga del Norte, Office of the Provincial Governor ZN Convention and Exhibition Center, Dipolog City Dear Governor Uy: S. 202Q This has reference to the letter you sent dated 29 August 2019, requesting for this Department's clarification on whether or not a provincial government needs to secure a government gratuitous permit in order to extract sand and gravel or quarry for the construction of infrastructure projects. In your letter, pursuant to pertinent provisions of Republic Act No. 7160 as amended, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code" ("LGC"), particularly Section 17, Section 17(b)(3)(iii), as well as relevant provisions of Republic Act No. 7942 otherwise known as "The Philippine Mining Act of 1995" (RA 7942) and its Implementing Rules and Regulationss, in connection with the relevant provisions9 of Department of Environment and Natural Resources ("DENR") Administrative Order (DAO) 92-30), expressly granted to the provincial governor the authority to issue and cancel permits on quarry, extract of sand and gravel, guano and gemstone gathering. Under this premise arose the request for clarification on whether or not a provincial government, though its provincial governor, as the issuing authority Of gratuitous permits, would still need to issue itself such permit before it can validly quarry or extract sand and gravel for its government projects. At the outset, this Department deems it imperative to cite no less than the 1987 Philippine Constitution itself, which states that: ARTICLE National Economy and Patrimony SECTION 2. xxx The exploration, development, and utilization of natural resources shall be control and supervision of the State: xxx Section 73, Implementing Rules and Regulations of the Philippine Mining Act of 1995 9 Sections 44 to 52, DENR Administrative Order (DAO) 92-30

The Congress may, by law, allow small-scale utilization of natural resources by Filipino citizens, as well as cooperative fish farming, with priority to subsistence fishermen and fishworkers in rivers, lakes, bays, and lagoons. [Emphasis and underscoring supplied]. Correspondingly, Section 4 of the RA 7942, provides that mineral resources are owned by the State and that, the exploration, utilization and processing thereof shall be under the State's full control and supervision, and that the State may directly undertake such activities. Likewise, Section 8 thereof provides that the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) shall be the primary government agency responsible for the conservation, management, development and proper use of the State's mineral resources. Further, while it is true that under Section 17(b)(3)(iii) of the LGCIO the enforcement of small scale mining law, and other laws on the protection of the environment has been devolved to the LGUs, note the proviso that such devolution is subject to supervision, control and review of the DENR, to wit: "(iii) Pursuant to national policies and subiect to. supervision, control and review of the DENR enforcement of forestry laws limited to community-based forestry projects, pollution control law, small-scale mining law, and other laws on the protection of the environment; and mini-hydro electric projects for local purposes" [Emphasis and underscoring supplied]. Evidently, the LGC did not fully devolve the enforcement of the small-scale mining law to the provincial government, as its enforcement is subject to the supervision, control and review of the DENR, which is in charge, subject to law and higher authority, of carrying out the State's constitutional mandate to control and supervise the exploration, development, utilization of the country's natural resources. Accordingly, this Department is of the considered view that a provincial government, despite being the issuing authority of gratuitous permits, would still need to apply for a such permit before it can validly quarry or extract sand and gravel for its government projects due to the fact that, ultimately, it is still the DENR which is responsible to implement and carry-out the Constitutional mandate to control and supervise the exploration, development, utilization and conservation of the country's natural resourcesll 10 Section 17(b)(3)(iii), Local Government Code of 1991, as amended. RA 7942 (The Philippine Mining Act Of 1995) Section 8 - The Department shall be the primary government agency responsible for the conservation, management, development, and proper use of the State's mineral resources including those in reservations, watershed areas, and lands of the public domain. Moreover, under Section Of DENR Administrative Order No. 2010-21 (DAO 2010-21) or the Implementing Rules and Regulations Of RA 7942, the LGUs' power to approve applications for mining permits not exceeding five (5) hectares, shall be in coordination with the Bureau/RegionaI Office(s) and is subject to valid and existing mining rights. In addition, the power devolved upon Provincial Governors/City Mayors to issue gratuitous permits, upon recommendation of the Provincial/City Mining Regulatory Board13, is subject to the DENR and the DENR Secretary's power to reverse, abrogate, nullify, void, or cancel such permits issued by the Provincial Governor14.
